about.title: Scotts Valley Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Scotts Valley is a small community tucked into the Santa Cruz Mountains, but its residents aren't immune to the risks posed by defective consumer goods, faulty auto parts, or unsafe equipment. With 16 injury collisions reported in the most recent final crash year, some involving vehicle component failures rather than driver error, product defects can factor into everyday incidents on corridors like SR-17, Scotts Valley Drive, and Glenwood Drive. Beyond the roadway, defective products in the home, workplace, or local businesses can cause serious harm just as easily. California law gives injured people a real path forward through strict liability claims, which don't require proving a manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and caused harm. If you've been hurt by a product in Scotts Valley, LawProactive can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who understands how these claims work locally.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Your Claim

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Negligence
items.desc: Because California applies strict liability to defective products, you generally only need to show the product was defective and caused your injury — not that the manufacturer was careless.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all be held liable under strict liability, which means an attorney can pursue every responsible link in the chain.

items.title: Preserving the Product Protects Your Claim
items.desc: Keeping the defective product intact and unaltered after an injury can be critical evidence, and an attorney can advise you on how to preserve it properly from the start.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: No. Under California's strict liability rules, you typically just need to show the product had a defect — in design, manufacturing, or warning — and that the defect caused your injury. This is different from most injury claims, which usually require proving fault.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, if possible, and avoid repairing or discarding it. The product itself is often key evidence, and an attorney can guide you on documenting and storing it safely.

items.question: Are product-related injuries common around Scotts Valley?
items.answer: Scotts Valley recorded 16 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, with reported crashes tending to cluster on Tuesdays between 3 and 5 p.m. along corridors like Mt Hermon Road and SR-17. While most crashes involve driver factors, some may involve defective vehicle parts, which is why it's worth having any suspected defect evaluated.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
